explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/229 with the Barth–Schneider positive answer. For any sequence of sets S_n ⊆ ℂ without finite limit points (derivedSet empty), there is a transcendental entire f such that each S_n (n ≥ 1) lies in the zero set of some derivative f^{(k_n)}. 'Transcendental' is encoded as transcendental over ℂ[X] acting by evaluation. For entire functions this is equivalent to being non-polynomial, since entire algebraic functions are polynomials. Formal proof linked.
